reviews.text: “I’m not gonna tell you their names… no, I’m not going to tell you their names… but if I did, I don’t think you’d sleep so well at night.” If I could describe this film in one word it would be TOPICAL. If it came out today I feel like it would either be the only thing people talked about or it would be so heavily censored that it wouldn’t even be released. The fact that Kubrick suddenly died from a heart attack just 4 days after a private screening is heartbreaking and also a bit strange? All respect to him, he’s a legend, but it definitely makes you wonder. I really enjoyed this film and was completely invested throughout. My only complaints are the pacing and how graphic it was. At times it genuinely felt like a miniseries the way it was paced. The amount of naked people was also just so uncomfortable 😭. I get that some of it is vital to the story and the nature of the secret society but it just felt sooo excessive at times. The score was so simple yet so haunting and the piano was so unsettling even just by alternating between two notes. This was definitely one of the most suspenseful films I’ve seen and it does a great job of putting you in every mysterious moment. The scene where he’s walking through the streets after he leaves Domino’s is absolutely brilliant, I was on the edge of my seat. Overall this was a great film and I can see why many would say that it’s Kubrick’s best. I loved the premise and think it’s such an interesting concept but there were just some minor things I didn’t like. If Letterboxd had a 3.75 stars option then I’d pick that.

Nessuno sa catturare l'anima e l'abisso umano attraverso gli occhi come Stanley Kubrick. È un viaggio tesissimo dentro le crepe di una coppia apparentemente indistruttibile, scossa dal dubbio e dalla tentazione di essere altro, per poi comprendere che essere "normali" non è una condanna ma una salvezza. Le scene della villa in maschera sono tra le più disturbanti e magnetiche mai girate; la nudità è abbondante ma di un'eleganza assoluta, priva di qualsiasi volgarità. L'ultimo atto costruisce una tensione paranoica soffocante, alimentata dalla lucida consapevolezza dell'impotenza individuale di fronte a poteri invisibili e inaccessibili. Prova maiuscola di Nicole Kidman e Tom Cruise — al netto di un doppiaggio italiano imbarazzante —, impreziosita da una recitazione complessa che risente positivamente delle reali tensioni dei due protagonisti. Da guardare, non da vedere.

Normally I would say some light-hearted things about the movie I just watched. And I’ll say same at the end, but for now I am going to keep things serious. Because this was a serious movie. The wheels in my head are still turning about the meaning behind what I’ve watched, below the surface of what we are told. It’s a dangerous movie, that is for sure. I can only imagine what was within the 40 cut minutes of this film, which were destroyed after Kubrick’s death. It almost feels like a warning to how the uppermost people of the world exist. It’s scary because it could be true. Key word “could”. Some films are scary because we know they are real somewhere, but this one is purely unknown. Alas, how unknown is it really, how far-fetched do the events in this film actually seem? This is what Kubrick seemed to want to show us with his final film. To tell us to keep our Eyes Wide Open in a corrupt world that thrives on us keeping them Shut. However, this what I feel could be an underlying theme. Obviously this film is based on an older novella as I discovered, which shares a different message. Just as interesting though. Tom Cruise did wonders in this film, can’t wait to see him in Digger. The ambiance was unbelievably tense, that piano was dreadful, in a good way. The dialogue and scenes were so encapsulating. Truly a work of art. Finally as promised, a lighter paragraph. If Die Hard and Gremlins are Christmas movies (for the record I think they both are), is Eyes Wide Shut as well? Food for thought.

Still such an amazing film, with incredible performances from Kidman and Cruise! I hate when people say sex shouldn’t be in films, because this movie makes a pretty strong argument for why it can be an important part of storytelling. It isn’t there just for the sake of being provocative; it actually plays an important role in the story, the characters, and the themes the film is exploring.I especially love watching Bill change throughout the film. Every time I rewatch it, I notice more about his journey and how the events of the night slowly challenge the way he sees himself, his marriage, and the world around him. Cruise does such a fantastic job showing that change. Kubrick’s direction is incredible, and there’s something so hypnotic about the way this entire movie is filmed. The atmosphere, the cinematography, the music, and the pacing all come together to create an experience that feels completely unique. Kidman and Cruise are both fantastic, and watching them share the screen makes the film even more fascinating. Their performances feel incredibly committed, and there’s so much going on beneath the surface of their characters. I also can’t help but think about how much of a financial risk a film like this would be today. A major studio probably wouldn’t take the same kind of chances on a movie this strange, slow, ambitious, and adult-oriented.
